Package gooeypainter

Class Painter

java.lang.Object
gooeypainter.Painter
public class Painter extends Object
A Painter lives on a grid of squares. It can move forward, turn left, pick up paint from paint buckets, and paint the square it is standing on.

Painter works the same way as the Painter in Code.org's Neighborhood, so code written on Code.org runs here with only the import changed. The grid comes from the grid.txt file in your project folder; see the package overview for its format.


 Painter p = new Painter(2, 3, "north", 5);   // at (2, 3), facing north, 5 paint
 p.paint("blue");                             // paints (2, 3); 4 paint left
 p.move();                                    // moves up to (2, 2)
 p.turnLeft();                                // now facing west

Location and direction

(0, 0) is the top-left square. x increases going right and y increases going down, so moving north subtracts 1 from y and moving south adds 1. A Painter always faces one of four directions: "north" (up), "east" (right), "south" (down), or "west" (left). Directions can be written with any capitalization.

Paint

A Painter carries its own supply of paint. Each call to paint(String) uses one unit. More paint can be picked up one unit at a time from paint buckets on the grid with takePaint(), or set directly with setPaint(int).

No turnRight()

A Painter can only turn left. That's on purpose: you can teach it to turn right (and much more) by writing your own class that extends Painter. See the package overview for an example.

Mistakes

Methods that can't do what they're asked either stop the program by throwing a GooeyPainterException or print a message and keep going. Each method below says which.

  • Constructor Details

    • Painter

      public Painter()
      Creates a Painter at (0, 0), facing east, with no paint.

      As on Code.org, a Painter made this way has unlimited paint when the grid is 20 or more squares wide. On smaller grids it starts with no paint, so it must pick some up with takePaint() or be given some with setPaint(int) before it can paint.

      If this is the first Painter in the program, the grid is loaded from grid.txt and the window opens.

      Throws:
      GooeyPainterException - if grid.txt has a mistake in it

    • Painter

      public Painter(int x, int y, String direction, int paint)
      Creates a Painter at a location of your choice, facing a direction of your choice, carrying a set amount of paint. 
      
 Painter artist = new Painter(0, 0, "east", 100);

      If this is the first Painter in the program, the grid is loaded from grid.txt and the window opens.

      Parameters:
      x - the column to start in, from 0 (the left edge) to the grid's width minus 1
      y - the row to start in, from 0 (the top edge) to the grid's height minus 1
      direction - the direction to face: "north", "east", "south", or "west" (any capitalization)
      paint - how many units of paint the Painter starts with
      Throws:
      GooeyPainterException - if (x, y) isn't on the grid, if the direction isn't one of the four above, or if grid.txt has a mistake in it

  • Method Details

    • turnLeft

      public void turnLeft()
      Turns the Painter 90 degrees to the left, without moving it.

      North turns to west, west to south, south to east, and east to north. Turning left three times is the same as turning right once.

    • move

      public void move()
      Moves the Painter one square forward in the direction it is facing.

      Moving onto a paint bucket or a painted square is fine. Moving off the edge of the grid or into an obstacle is not: it stops the program. Use canMove() first if you aren't sure the way is clear:

      
 while (p.canMove()) {
     p.move();
 }
      Throws:
      GooeyPainterException - if the square ahead is off the grid or is an obstacle

    • paint

      public void paint(String color)
      Paints the square the Painter is standing on, using one unit of paint. Painting a square that is already painted replaces its old color. 
      
 p.paint("red");        // a web color name
 p.paint("SkyBlue");    // capital letters don't matter
 p.paint("#FF8800");    // a hex code, such as one from pixilart.com

      If the Painter has no paint, nothing is painted, the message "There is no more paint in the painter's bucket" is printed, and the program keeps going. Use hasPaint() to check first.

      Parameters:
      color - one of the 140 web color names (such as "red", "gold", "skyblue", "darkgreen"), or a hex code in the form "#RRGGBB" or "#RGB"
      Throws:
      GooeyPainterException - if the color isn't recognized, or if the square has a paint bucket on it

    • scrapePaint

      public void scrapePaint()
      Removes the paint from the square the Painter is standing on, turning it back into plain grass. This doesn't give the Painter any paint back.

      If the square has no paint on it, the message "There's no paint to remove here" is printed and the program keeps going. Use isOnPaint() to check first.

    • takePaint

      public void takePaint()
      Takes one unit of paint from the paint bucket the Painter is standing on and adds it to the Painter's own supply. The number on the bucket goes down by 1, and when it reaches 0 the bucket disappears.

      To take all of the paint from a bucket:

      
 while (p.isOnBucket()) {
     p.takePaint();
 }

      If there is no bucket here, the message "There is no paint to collect here" is printed and the program keeps going.

    • hidePainter

      public void hidePainter()
      Hides the Painter so the squares under it can be seen. A hidden Painter can still move, turn, and paint; you just can't see it. A good way to end a pixel art program is to hide the Painter so the whole picture shows.
      See Also:
      • showPainter()

    • showPainter

      public void showPainter()
      Shows the Painter again after hidePainter().

    • hideBuckets

      public void hideBuckets()
      Hides every paint bucket on the grid. The buckets are still there and still hold paint; they just aren't drawn. This affects all buckets, not only the one under this Painter.

      Code.org's Painter has this method but leaves it out of its documentation.

      See Also:
      • showBuckets()

    • showBuckets

      public void showBuckets()
      Shows every paint bucket on the grid again after hideBuckets().

      Code.org's Painter has this method but leaves it out of its documentation.

    • setPaint

      public void setPaint(int paint)
      Sets how much paint the Painter is carrying, replacing whatever it had.

      If paint is negative, nothing changes and the message "Paint amount must not be a negative number." is printed. A Painter with unlimited paint (see Painter()) ignores this method.

      Parameters:
      paint - the new number of units of paint, 0 or more

    • getMyPaint

      public int getMyPaint()
      Returns how many units of paint the Painter is carrying.

      For a Painter with unlimited paint (see Painter()), this counts down below 0 as it paints, the same as on Code.org; use hasPaint() to check whether a Painter can paint.

      Returns:
      the number of units of paint in the Painter's bucket

    • isOnBucket

      public boolean isOnBucket()
      Checks whether the Painter is standing on a paint bucket that still has paint in it. (Empty buckets disappear, so this is the same as asking whether takePaint() would work here.)
      Returns:

    • getColor

      public String getColor()
      Returns the color of the square the Painter is standing on, written exactly the way it was given to paint(String). For example, after paint("Red") this returns "Red", not "red". 
      
 if (p.isOnPaint() && p.getColor().equals("red")) {
     p.scrapePaint();
 }
      Returns:
      the color of this square, or null if it isn't painted

    • canMove

      public boolean canMove()
      Checks whether the Painter can move forward one square in the direction it is facing, without actually moving. Call this before move() to avoid stopping the program by running into an edge or obstacle.
      Returns:
      true if the square ahead is on the grid and isn't an obstacle

    • canMove

      public boolean canMove(String direction)
      Checks whether the Painter could move one square in the given direction, without turning or moving. For example, canMove("north") checks the square above the Painter, whichever way it is facing.
      Parameters:
      direction - the direction to check: "north", "east", "south", or "west" (any capitalization)
      Returns:
      true if the square in that direction is on the grid and isn't an obstacle
      Throws:
      GooeyPainterException - if the direction isn't one of the four above
